old_row.rationale: Proverbs aims to give perception to the innocent and the young; the psalm says the disclosure of God's words gives understanding to the simple. Both describe instruction benefiting inexperienced hearers.

new_row.rationale: The proverbs give resourcefulness and perception to the innocent and the young; the psalm says the disclosure of God's words gives light and understanding to the simple. Both connect instruction with increased perception or understanding, while preserving the different descriptions of its recipients.

old_row.rationale: Wisdom describes repeatedly calling without obedience; Isaiah's judgment likewise answers the failure to obey when the Lord called and the disregard shown when He spoke.

new_row.rationale: Wisdom describes repeatedly calling without obedience; Isaiah's judgment likewise answers the failure to obey when the Lord called and the disregard shown when He spoke.

old_row.rationale: Applying the ear to wisdom and the heart to understanding is echoed by the commands to apply the ear to the father's words and keep them in the heart.

new_row.rationale: The earlier assurance that the ear will obey wisdom and the learner will apply the heart to understanding corresponds to the later commands to apply the ear to the father's words and keep them in the heart.

old_row.rationale: Seeking wisdom as silver and hidden treasure is complemented by the later valuation of trading in wisdom above treasures of gold and silver.

new_row.rationale: Seeking wisdom as silver and treasures is complemented by the later valuation of trading in wisdom above treasures of gold and silver.

old_row.rationale: The Lord shields the journey of those acting rightly; the psalm combines God's blameless way with His being a protector of all who hope in Him.

new_row.rationale: The Lord will shield the journey of those acting rightly; the psalm says the Lord directs a person's steps and supports his hand so that when he falls he will not be dashed down. The comparison connects divine care with the person's course and protection from falling ruin.

old_row.rationale: The removal of ungodly and lawless people from the land corresponds to the psalm's destruction of evildoers and inheritance of the land by those waiting for the Lord.

old_row.rationale: Fearless sitting and pleasant sleep correspond to the psalmist lying down and sleeping in peace because the Lord makes him dwell in hope.

new_row.rationale: Fearless sitting and pleasant sleep correspond to the psalmist's resolve to lie down and sleep in peace because the Lord made him dwell alone in hope.

old_row.rationale: Freedom from approaching fright and ungodly assaults is paired with the righteous person's lack of fear at an evil report and established heart while facing enemies.
